header:
Meeting: POC Weekly Sync - Reliability Incident Follow-up
Date: 2026-03-03
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (Redwood CSM), Maya Chen (Catalyst Eng Manager), Daniel Ortiz (Catalyst SRE), Sana Rahman (Catalyst Product), Chris Valdez (Catalyst Dev)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on the recent reliability incidents (timeouts, 5xxs, rate limits). Reviewed incident timeline, probable causes (burst traffic + autoscaler lag + retry storms), short-term mitigations (rate limit tuning, client-side backoff, failover route), and medium-term options (dedicated capacity, routing policies, circuit-breaker). Agreed next steps to share logs, run load tests, and schedule runbook deep-dive.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we wanted to use this time to go through the incident from thursday and align on mitigations and next steps.
[00:12] Maya Chen: Thanks, Alex. short version — we had a spike around 14:22 UTC, a bunch of timeouts and intermittent 5xx. Our users saw errors on the search flow.
[00:22] Daniel Ortiz: yeah, we saw an uptick in 504 and 502s, and client retries basically amplified the load. we were also hitting the rate-limit threshold on our shared API key.
[00:34] Priya Patel: ok that's helpful. quick question — are you using the hosted route with auto-scaling, or did you have any dedicated capacity pinned for this test?
[00:44] Chris Valdez: We were on hosted, default settings. no dedicated capacity.
[00:49] Priya Patel: got it. so autoscaler is the likely place to look but also client retries and backoff. sometimes the client library will do aggressive retries and that turns a transient 5xx into a bigger outage.
[01:05] Maya Chen: we do have our own retry wrapper; it's set to 3 retries with fixed 500ms backoff. we were wondering whether we should change to exponential backoff.
[01:17] Priya Patel: yes, we usually recommend exponential backoff with jitter. also add a circuit-breaker so after N failures you stop retrying for some time. that prevents retry storms from overwhelming the autoscaler.
[01:30] Alex Morgan: quick note — during the spike our telemetry shows latency went from 120ms median to 800ms p95 and p99 spiked beyond 3s for certain model routes.
[01:42] Jordan Li: and we saw error rate climb to ~7% for a 15-minute window, which is above your SLA target right?
[01:49] Maya Chen: yes that's above our SLO. that's what triggered ops pages.
[01:54] Daniel Ortiz: i captured traces — there's a tail of requests that clipped the GPU queue. it looks like requests stacked up and we had some 5xx from the runtime when memory throttled.
[02:08] Priya Patel: that matches a scenario where the model variant hits memory pressure — sometimes GPU OOM leads to 5xx. was there any model switching or quantization variant active?
[02:18] Chris Valdez: we pinned to the small-llama-quant variant. nothing dynamic.
[02:23] Priya Patel: ok so likely autoscaler + queued requests + client retry storm. also the rate-limit policy happened to be at a lower threshold — the gateway started returning 429s once the shared rate bucket was exhausted.
[02:36] Alex Morgan: to be clear, we also saw some 502s in the gateway that coincide with the autoscaler scale-up lag. when instances are cold starting there can be a brief window where capacity is low.
[02:47] Maya Chen: timeline please — can you share exact timestamps for the scale events?
[02:51] Priya Patel: yes we'll extract the event timeline and share logs. action: we'll dump the tail traces and the scale events.
[03:00] Daniel Ortiz: another data point — our infra also ran spike tests internally at 14:15 which may have contributed. mixing two spikes is rough.
[03:09] Alex Morgan: ok. let's go over mitigation levels — short term (minutes-hours), mid term (days), long term (weeks).
[03:16] Priya Patel: short term: set client-side exponential backoff with jitter, reduce retry attempts to 1-2, and add a simple circuit-breaker. also temporarily increase the hosted rate-limit for your API key while we run controlled tests — we can open a temporary burst window.
[03:33] Maya Chen: are there cost implications to increasing burst windows?
[03:36] Alex Morgan: small, but yes there could be incremental usage. we'll estimate.
[03:40] Priya Patel: mid-term: we can provision dedicated capacity or reserved burst capacity for predictable throughput. that gives you guaranteed headroom and eliminates scale cold-starts for critical routes. we can also tune the autoscaler thresholds and latency-based routing for these routes.
[03:57] Daniel Ortiz: what about retries server-side? does Redwood have server-side rate shaping or request queueing options?
[04:04] Priya Patel: we have queueing and KV prefix caching, and we can enable graceful tail-dropping on overload for specific routes, but we generally recommend client-side throttling as first defense. server-side shaping is possible for Dedicated or Private customers with custom policies.
[04:20] Chris Valdez: you mentioned KV cache — we did enable prefix cache but our hit rate was low; maybe our prompt patterns are too variable.
[04:28] Priya Patel: yes that will reduce effectiveness. we can help identify stable prefixes to boost cache hit.
[04:33] Jordan Li: also platforms-level fallback — on overload we can route to a smaller model variant for non-critical calls to preserve availability. that's an automatic fallback we can set per-route.
[04:46] Maya Chen: that could work for our background scoring calls. for the user-facing search, quality matters.
[04:54] Alex Morgan: technical deep-dive on root cause: autoscaler lag plus retry amplification plus rate-limit exhaustion. next steps — we'll produce a timeline and propose a config (retries, circuit-breaker, rate-limit bump) and suggested runbook edits.
[05:10] Daniel Ortiz: a question about logs — do you have request ids we can correlate with our traces?
[05:15] Priya Patel: yes every request has request_id and trace_id; we'll share the map. sometimes the transcription in our logs says "r id" or similar in the export but the id's there.
[05:25] Maya Chen: also want to review alerting thresholds — our SRE got paged at 5% error rate; maybe we tune to 2% for staging and 1% for prod.
[05:34] Jordan Li: agreed. we can help propose alert thresholds per environment.
[05:38] Chris Valdez: what about long-term — do we need to move to Dedicated to guarantee no noisy neighbors?
[05:44] Alex Morgan: Dedicated reduces noisy neighbor risk and gives predictable throughput. downside is cost and onboarding time if you want on-prem private. for many teams a hybrid approach works — keep core critical routes on Dedicated and others on hosted.
[05:58] Daniel Ortiz: do you support automatic fallback to a smaller model if larger variant fails?
[06:02] Priya Patel: yes we can configure routing policies that fallback to a compatible smaller variant. that maintains availability at lower quality. we can include that in the runbook.
[06:12] Maya Chen: ok let's capture immediate actions.
[06:15] Alex Morgan: quick recap — Redwood will: 1) provide incident timeline and request traces; 2) propose retry/circuit-breaker config; 3) temporarily open a burst rate window; 4) propose Dedicated/reserved options and cost estimate. Catalyst will: run load tests, adjust client retry logic, and confirm stakeholders for runbook review. does that sound right?
[06:33] Maya Chen: yes. please add estimated cost for burst and dedicated so we can present to finance.
[06:39] Alex Morgan: will do.
[06:41] Sana Rahman: small note — product would like prioritized UX-friendly error messages when we are degraded versus showing generic failures.
[06:48] Priya Patel: good point — we can add a header in responses when degraded mode is active so you can show a softer message.
[06:55] Chris Valdez: and for telemetry we want more granular tail-latency histograms per route — can you increase retention for the POC?
[07:03] Jordan Li: we can bump observability retention for the pilot temporarily; we'll include that in the follow up.
[07:09] Maya Chen: any blockers to do the short-term changes this week?
[07:12] Priya Patel: none from our side. we need traces and traffic profile to tune the thresholds.
[07:17] Daniel Ortiz: we'll upload traffic profile by Friday.
[07:20] Alex Morgan: great. final check — security/compliance questions? nothing new?
[07:25] Maya Chen: still want SOC2 doc and KMS integration notes for Dedicated, but that's separate thread.
[07:31] Alex Morgan: we'll send SOC2 and KMS integration doc after the call.
[07:35] Jordan Li: ok i'm going to schedule the runbook deep-dive for 2026-03-10 and send calendar invites.
[07:40] Maya Chen: thanks everyone.
[07:43] Alex Morgan: thanks all, we'll follow up with the logs and proposed configs.
[07:47] [Meeting ends]
